page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6e-c12g1.3xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and designed for deep learning inference, model evaluation, and scientific computing. It features 12 vCPUs derived from 6 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions and AES acceleration. Host memory capacity totals 92.0 GB, yielding 7.67 GB per virtual core, alongside a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by a dedicated NVIDIA Volta V100 GPU equipped with 32 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. The instance includes no bundled local storage, necessitating external network-attached volumes for operating systems and persistent datasets. Benchmark results demonstrate strong GPU throughput, with prompt processing reaching 17,451.87 tokens per second on a 135M parameter language model and 1,350.18 tokens per second on a 7B model. Generation speeds achieve 114.19 tokens per second on 7B models, placing its inference throughput in top tiers.

Host CPU performance remains moderate to weak in comparative testing, posting 897.0 in Geekbench single-core and 4,736.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside an average PassMark CPU score of 9,968.09. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth measures 56.53 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 48.87 GB/sec. Given its hardware balance, the instance provides cost-effective throughput for GPU-centric execution where single-thread host CPU speed and direct local NVMe storage are not primary bottlenecks.

The ecs.gn6e-c12g1.3xlarge instance is best suited for machine learning inference, medium-scale deep learning model fine-tuning, computer vision pipelines, and accelerated mathematical simulations requiring 32 GB of GPU VRAM.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6e-c12g1.3xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance configured with 12 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, 92.0 GB of system RAM, and a single NVIDIA Volta V100 GPU containing 32 GB of VRAM. It operates on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps, though it bundles no local disk storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional performance in deep learning inference, recording top-tier speeds of 1,350.18 tokens per second for prompt processing and 114.19 tokens per second for generation on 7B parameter language models. Host CPU benchmarks demonstrate average multi-core and weak single-core capabilities, making the instance an efficient choice primarily for GPU-bound workloads such as neural network inference, computer vision processing, and accelerated matrix computations where heavy local IOPS are not essential.
